not_found: Congressional Record issue coverage was refreshed on 2026-11-13 and runs through the 2026-11-12 issue (387 issues across Vol. 171–172). One Van Hollen item is from the November 9, 2026 issue.
Quotes were verified in freshly fetched Congressional Record HTM speaker turns using case-sensitive ALL-CAPS speaker tags, so mid-speech mentions such as “Mr. Hawley.” were not treated as new turns.

Angus S. King, Jr., had no independently checkable first-person future-action promises in the Record, and no sufficiently clear official X promise was used. Josh Hawley and Elissa Slotkin had few or no such Record promises; verified official X posts were used as a medium fallback for those commitments only. Floor speeches still make up most items.

Ten independently checkable first-person future-action promises per senator could not be substantiated without reclassifying statements. Appeals, support or opposition, and priorities were retained only as statements.
Amy Klobuchar’s ICE funding pledge appears in a vote-explanation statement; it is included because it is a first-person future-action commitment, not a purely procedural remark.

S. 1829 (STOP CSAM Act of 2025) is named on the same Congressional Record page as Hawley’s remarks about “this bill,” in the unanimous-consent heading and the preceding debate. S. 3904 was the housing bill Van Hollen was introducing, but the number is not in his spoken text, so it was not assigned.
No written Q&A included. No items with brackets.
